items.title: 68533_Sam Jones oral history interview
items.q: Interviewer mentions Coleman Hawkins in the context of comparing styles with Lester Young; Interviewee does not claim personal interaction, only acknowledges Hawkins as a stylist with a following.

ctx.x: --and going into the scat singing kind of thing--would you agree that in talking about jazz and just looking at the various periods, what it, how the music evolved would you agree that in each of those periods that there seemed to be, like--OK, take into like we mentioned, Louis Armstrong that there were certain techniques that he utilizes, the way he approached improvisation that sort of outlined himself as an individual--artist and that sort of sets the guidelines or parameters, you know, like from which the…

like, approaches to harmony, approaches to melody and approaches to rhythm that seem to be, um, a part of each of those particular years. Like you mentioned the swing years, certain way that Lester Young approached the melody, certain way...Hawkins approached melody, certain way Dizzy Gillespie or Miles or Charlie Parker---- in terms of what identifies their style, would you say that is what makes the difference within the music? Can that be used to in terms of defining what jazz is about?

It could be, and it could, and then again I-I'm not, see, see like uh, like I said in the (inaudible) a variety of style of music. Uh, like we had the blues when I was a kid coming up. OK, and you had, you--then you had the uh, you had your country and westerns, you know, that's a strong music--country and western--don't let nobody, uh, kid you about that.
